doc.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

title: Playing cello now and the long gap from the late 1970s
summary: His hands hurt now; he barely played for 25-30 years while running a studio and making youth R&B records in the 1980s.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Is it harder to play now than it was when you were 17?

Oh my God no comparison. My hands hurt, and my bow arm's nowhere near as good. But you know there was a period of time when I didn't really play every day all the time. So it's like I can't expect — I gave that up to have a different kind of career. And I would say from the late '70s I really didn't play until you know maybe there were probably about 25—30 years that I didn't play even on a day to day level. You know? I ran a studio, I had employees, I tried to hustle. In the '80s I made a lot of what I call youth R&B records. The '80s were very popular, the kids singing. So I made a record with a 14— year—old or a 16—year—old group or a 17—year. You know? I mean and it involved a lot of hours and you were exhausted just pulling teeth and getting the records done on time and making them try to be good.
